BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Review of the Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## Headline

The Seller's package departs from our playbook on nearly every material point. The most significant problem is structural. Three provisions, read together, would quietly put fundamental, title and fraud claims under the general regime and would let the Seller escape almost any claim:

- the "all Claims" limitation and non-reliance language (cl. 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 / 13);
- whole-data-room and public-register disclosure; and
- a blanket buyer-knowledge bar.

Several Seller statements present positions as "addressed", "agreed", "settled" or "adequate". None of them is agreed. We should treat the whole document as an opening position.

**Two warnings on our own fallbacks:**

- The Seller's **20% / AUD 4.8m cap** and **18-month claims period** match our fallbacks exactly. **Neither is cleared.** Both need Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft, and none has been given. A number matching a fallback does not clear it.
- The Disclosure Letter is stated **as at 22 September 2026**. Today is 5 November 2026. Every factual item (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses) needs a refresh before we rely on it. The Seller should be asked to confirm what has changed, and we should distinguish verified updates from assertions.

---

## Issue-by-issue analysis

### 1. General Warranty cap (cl. 12.1)
- **Seller:** 20% / AUD 4.8m.
- **Playbook:** 25% / AUD 6.0m opening. 20% is a conditional fallback only, with Amelia Frost's prior written authority.
- **Analysis:** The cap cannot be assessed in isolation. At 20%, combined with the Seller's thresholds, disclosure and knowledge positions, our real protection would be far lower than the headline number suggests.
- **Push back:** Counter at **25% / AUD 6.0m**. Do not signal any 20% fallback. If the deal team wants to use it, escalate to Amelia Frost for written authority referencing SPA-003 and this Seller Update draft. It should be considered only as part of a package that fixes items 3 to 7 below.

### 2. Thresholds (cl. 12.2)
- **Seller:** de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; only the excess is recoverable (a deductible).
- **Playbook:** de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; **first-dollar recovery once exceeded** (a tipping basket).
- **Analysis:** These are five times our levels, and the deductible structure would permanently absorb AUD 250k of loss. Together with a AUD 25k de minimis, many realistic claims (privacy remediation, single customer credits, contract leakage) would never be recoverable.
- **Push back:** Reinstate AUD 5k / AUD 50k with a tipping basket. Confirm that related claims aggregate for de minimis purposes. Confirm that thresholds do not apply to Fundamental, Title, Tax, specific indemnities or fraud.

### 3. Claims period and the "all Claims" limitation spread (cl. 12.3 / 13)
- **Seller:** 18 months for general claims, *and* "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
- **Playbook:** 24 months. 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost's approval, which has not been given. Fundamental/Title claims get at least six years. Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories must stay separate with **no hidden general-regime override**.
- **Analysis:** The second sentence is the real problem. It is a default-override. It would pull indemnities, Tax, IP, purchase price and covenant claims into the general limitations unless each is expressly carved out. Any drafting gap would then favour the Seller.
- **Push back:** Counter at 24 months. Delete the "applies to all Claims" sentence. Reverse the default so that general limitations apply **only** to General Warranty Claims, and each other category has its own regime.

### 4. Fundamental / Title / Capacity
- **Seller:** Same caps and time limits as general warranties, "for administrative simplicity."
- **Playbook:** Separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Analysis:** This is a significant departure. Title to 100% of the shares is the core of what we are buying. Limiting title recovery to AUD 4.8m on a AUD 24m price is not an administrative matter.
- **Push back:** Reject outright. Fundamental and Title warranties get a 100% cap (AUD 24m), a minimum of six years, and no thresholds, disclosure against them or knowledge qualifier.

### 5. Fraud carve-out (cl. 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature."
- **Playbook:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct are carved out of **all** caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- **Analysis:** As drafted, the clause purports to limit fraud claims. This is a non-negotiable point. We have no authority to concede it, and nobody on our side can.
- **Push back:** Insert an express carve-out that overrides everything else, covering the Seller, its Related Bodies Corporate and its officers, employees and advisers. Confirm that non-reliance does not exclude misleading or deceptive conduct claims to the extent that cannot lawfully be excluded.

### 6. Disclosure (Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter paras 1.1 and 1.2)
- **Seller:** Discloses the entire data room (including DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, the statutory registers and all publicly searchable records. Para 1.2 says this is "without limiting" the specific disclosures.
- **Playbook:** Specific fair disclosure only. Reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Analysis:** General disclosure would neutralise the warranties in practice, because almost any issue is somewhere in the data room. The specific disclosures in paras 2 to 10 actually show the Seller can disclose specifically. Para 1.4 (non-admission) is acceptable in principle. However, it must not dilute specific indemnities or allow the Seller to argue that a disclosed matter is not a breach.
- **Push back:**
  - Delete paras 1.1 and 1.2.
  - Disclosure is effective only if it is fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter, and is made against a specific warranty.
  - No disclosure against Fundamental/Title warranties, Tax covenants or specific indemnities.
  - Add a clause confirming that disclosure does not prejudice any specific indemnity.

### 7. Buyer knowledge (cl. 8.3)
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter known to the Buyer *or its advisers*, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records.
- **Playbook:** Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any knowledge qualifier must use named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry. It must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Analysis:** This is constructive knowledge on top of general disclosure. Combined with item 6, it is a near-total bar. It would also arguably defeat the indemnities we are asking for precisely *because* we know about the issues (Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses).
- **Push back:** Delete cl. 8.3. If any knowledge concept survives, it should apply only to the Seller's warranties, qualified "so far as the Seller is aware". "Aware" should mean the actual knowledge of named individuals after reasonable enquiry. Add an express "no buyer knowledge" clause.

### 8. Bluefen consent (cl. 3 / 6.3)
- **Facts:** Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue (around 30%). Change-control consent is under cl. 11.2, with conditions in cl. 11.3. Disclosure para 2 confirms that **no final consent and no evidence of satisfied conditions** existed as at 22 September.
- **Seller:** Says the consent is "addressed", but offers only reasonable endeavours, with the condition treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent.
- **Analysis:** "Addressed" contradicts the Seller's own disclosure. Consent-on-delivery ignores the cl. 11.3 conditions. A conditional consent that is never satisfied could still allow Bluefen to terminate after Completion. Reasonable endeavours is inadequate for a 30% customer.
- **Push back:**
  - Make it a Condition Precedent that is satisfied only by (a) an effective, unconditional (or conditions-satisfied) written consent from Bluefen, in a form reasonably acceptable to the Buyer, **and** (b) evidence that the cl. 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
  - The Condition should be waivable only by the Buyer.
  - Seller obligation upgraded beyond reasonable endeavours.
  - Request the current status of the consent now.

### 9. Riverlark facility (cl. 2 / 7)
- **Facts:** About AUD 3.2m outstanding (an approximate figure). Change-control is under cl. 8.1, discharge under cl. 9.2. Disclosure para 3 says the facility has not been repaid and no discharge is included.
- **Seller:** The release is to be provided after Completion.
- **Analysis:** A post-Completion release means we would complete with security still registered over the target. The change-control clause may also be triggered by Completion itself.
- **Push back:**
  - As Completion deliverables, require a current payout letter (a figure as at Completion, with daily interest), direct repayment from Completion funds, and executed deeds of release, PPSR releases and any mortgage or security discharges.
  - Treat the payout amount as Debt in the debt-free/cash-free mechanics.
  - A post-Completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark **and** Amelia Frost's approval. Neither exists.
  - Do not rely on the "approximately AUD 3.2m" figure. Get the payout letter.

### 10. DD-005 employee bonuses / funds flow
- **Facts:** AUD 420,000 in conditional Completion bonuses. Disclosure para 5 confirms they are **not** in the funds flow, and says nothing on payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs.
- **Seller:** The funds flow "reflects the agreed price mechanics", with bonuses described as "a matter for the Seller."
- **Analysis:** The price mechanics are not agreed. If the Company pays the bonuses after Completion, the cost falls on us. "A matter for the Seller" is not a legal obligation. On-costs (payroll tax, superannuation, possibly workers' compensation) could add a material amount on top of AUD 420k. This is exactly the silent exclusion the playbook targets.
- **Push back:**
  - Either (a) include AUD 420k plus all triggered on-costs as a specific line item in the funds flow, treated as Debt or a Transaction Expense deducted from the price and paid through payroll at Completion; or (b) make them expressly Seller-funded, with an indemnity.
  - Require confirmation of the on-cost calculation.
  - Remove "agreed" from any description of the funds flow.

### 11. Ironquay IP (cl. 11.1)
- **Facts:** DD-004 cl. 7.3 makes transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials conditional on cleared payment of all SOW3 fees. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open. That is not independent proof either way. There is no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment.
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is "adequate."
- **Analysis:** Paying AUD 180k may not resolve the issue. The real risk is that the Company does not own the SOW3 Project Materials. That creates infringement, ownership and remediation exposure well beyond the fee.
- **Push back:**
  - Broaden the indemnity to cover all loss arising from any failure of the Company to own, or hold a sufficient licence to, the Ironquay deliverables. That includes third-party claims and re-development or remediation costs.
  - Keep the SOW3 cure: the Seller procures cleared payment, with evidence, and a confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay, ideally pre-Completion.
  - Keep this outside the general cap, thresholds and knowledge bar.
  - Do not concede that AUD 180k is owed or paid. Verify with bank evidence or Ironquay confirmation.

### 12. DD-006 export / privacy incident (cl. 4.6 / Schedule 6)
- **Facts:** A download link was sent to an unintended external address. The export may contain about 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, timestamps). It is not established whether anyone accessed the file, what the exact scope is, or whether notification is required. The investigation is preliminary.
- **Seller:** "Not expected to be material."
- **Analysis:** That characterisation is unsupported, so we should not accept it. Equally, we must **not** overstate the matter. There is no confirmed breach, harm, notification obligation or quantified loss, and we should not demand a numeric amount. The right approach is process protection while the facts develop.
- **Push back:**
  - Pre-Completion covenants: preserve all logs and evidence, continue a proper investigation (consider independent forensic review), give the Buyer regular updates and access, and make no notification decisions or regulator or individual communications without consultation.
  - Require an assessment under the Privacy Act eligible data breach regime to be completed or progressed.
  - Delete the "not material" language.
  - Seek a specific indemnity for loss arising from the incident, regardless of disclosure, without assuming any outcome.
  - Request an updated status, since the information is six weeks old.

### 13. Sandbar supplier renewals (AUD 330,000)
- **Facts:** Three related renewals of AUD 110k each. The disclosure does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Seller:** "Ordinary-course operating costs."
- **Analysis:** This is an assertion. The playbook says to assess the renewals and neither classify them automatically as Debt nor demand a price deduction.
- **Push back:** Request the DD-008 and DD-011 contracts and the timing, scope, termination rights and accrual treatment, and confirm whether they were approved within budget and authority. Reserve our position on classification (ordinary course, Transaction Expense or Debt) pending that review. Do not concede "ordinary course" in the SPA.

### 14. Tax / IP warranties
- **Seller:** "Settled under the general regime."
- **Playbook:** OPEN. There is no resolution, and we are not assuming unlimited liability.
- **Push back:** Reject "settled". Tax and IP remain open items for separate negotiation, with their own regime (for example, a tax covenant with appropriate time limits) outside the general cap and thresholds. Make no concession that they fall under the general regime.

### 15. Title evidence
- **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the share register at DD-012.
- **Analysis:** DD-012 is an internal source supplied by the Seller. Disclosure para 10 itself acknowledges we have not verified it.
- **Push back:** Require independent evidence: an ASIC company extract and historical search consistent with the register, PPSR searches against the Seller and the Company, share certificates, and evidence of the issue and transfer history (including no options, convertibles or rights). Also require board and shareholder authority for the Seller, any security trustee or lender releases over the shares, and a clean title, capacity and authority warranty within the Fundamental regime.

### 16. Lower-priority confirmations
- **Office lease (DD-007):** Notification only, per the disclosure. Confirm independently, diarise the notice as a Completion deliverable, and confirm there is no change-of-control default.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** The assignment restriction is described as not triggered by a share sale. Verify against the clause text, including any change-of-control or deemed-assignment wording.

---

## Summary of recommendations

| # | Item | Seller position | Our response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | General cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | Counter 25% / AUD 6.0m. 20% is **not authorised** without Amelia Frost's written approval |
| 2 | Thresholds | AUD 25k / AUD 250k deductible | AUD 5k / AUD 50k, tipping basket from first dollar |
| 3 | Claims period | 18 months; limits apply to all Claims | 24 months; delete the "all Claims" override; 18 months not authorised |
| 4 | Fundamental/Title | Same as general | 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside thresholds, disclosure and knowledge |
| 5 | Fraud | Limited like everything else | Full carve-out from everything. Non-negotiable |
| 6 | Disclosure | Whole data room plus public records | Specific fair disclosure only |
| 7 | Buyer knowledge | Blanket bar incl. advisers and constructive knowledge | Delete; any qualifier limited to named Seller persons with reasonable enquiry |
| 8 | Bluefen | Reasonable endeavours; consent on delivery | CP: effective consent **and** evidence that cl. 11.3 conditions are met |
| 9 | Riverlark | Post-Completion release | Payout letter, repayment from funds, releases at Completion |
| 10 | Bonuses | Excluded from funds flow | AUD 420k plus on-costs as a line item or Seller-funded with indemnity |
| 11 | Ironquay | Narrow SOW3 indemnity | Broad IP indemnity plus SOW3 cure; AUD 180k unverified |
| 12 | DD-006 | "Not material" | Preserve logs, investigate, update covenants, specific indemnity; no assumed breach |
| 13 | Sandbar | Ordinary course | Assess; reserve classification |
| 14 | Tax/IP | "Settled" | Open; separate regime |
| 15 | Title | DD-012 register | Independent title, encumbrance and authority evidence |

**Process points for the deal team:**

1. **Do not concede the 20% cap or the 18-month period.** They match our fallbacks but are uncleared. If anyone wants to use either, seek Amelia Frost's written authority identifying this draft (the Seller Update draft and SPA-003), and use it only as part of a package that fixes items 3 to 7.
2. **Reject the characterisations.** The Seller's uses of "addressed", "agreed price mechanics", "adequate", "settled", "not material" and "ordinary course" are assertions. In several places (Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses) they are contradicted by the Seller's own Disclosure Letter.
3. **Refresh the facts.** The Disclosure Letter is dated 22 September 2026. Send a written request for current status on Bluefen, the Riverlark payout, Ironquay payment and assignment, the DD-006 investigation, the bonus on-costs and the Sandbar contracts. Record which updates are verified and which are Seller assertions.
4. **Prioritise in the mark-up.** The structural provisions come first, because they undermine everything else: the fraud carve-out, Fundamental/Title separation, deletion of the "all Claims" override, specific disclosure and deletion of the buyer-knowledge bar. Then the Completion deliverables (Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses), then the economic terms.

This is a negotiation analysis, not formal legal advice. The final mark-up should be settled by the responsible NSW-qualified lawyers on the deal team.

### 5. Fraud carve-out (cl. 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature."
- **Playbook:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct are carved out of **all** caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- **Analysis:** As drafted, the clause purports to limit fraud claims. This is a non-negotiable point. We have no authority to concede it, and nobody on our side can.
- **Push back:** Insert an express carve-out that overrides everything else, covering the Seller, its Related Bodies Corporate and its officers, employees and advisers. Confirm that non-reliance does not exclude misleading or deceptive conduct claims to the extent that cannot lawfully be excluded.

### 6. Disclosure (Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter paras 1.1 and 1.2)
- **Seller:** Discloses the entire data room (including DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, the statutory registers and all publicly searchable records. Para 1.2 says this is "without limiting" the specific disclosures.
- **Playbook:** Specific fair disclosure only. Reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Analysis:** General disclosure would neutralise the warranties in practice, because almost any issue is somewhere in the data room. The specific disclosures in paras 2 to 10 actually show the Seller can disclose specifically. Para 1.4 (non-admission) is acceptable in principle. However, it must not dilute specific indemnities or allow the Seller to argue that a disclosed matter is not a breach.
- **Push back:**
  - Delete paras 1.1 and 1.2.
  - Disclosure is effective only if it is fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter, and is made against a specific warranty.
  - No disclosure against Fundamental/Title warranties, Tax covenants or specific indemnities.
  - Add a clause confirming that disclosure does not prejudice any specific indemnity.

### 7. Buyer knowledge (cl. 8.3)
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter known to the Buyer *or its advisers*, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records.
- **Playbook:** Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any knowledge qualifier must use named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry. It must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Analysis:** This is constructive knowledge on top of general disclosure. Combined with item 6, it is a near-total bar. It would also arguably defeat the indemnities we are asking for precisely *because* we know about the issues (Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses).
- **Push back:** Delete cl. 8.3. If any knowledge concept survives, it should apply only to the Seller's warranties, qualified "so far as the Seller is aware". "Aware" should mean the actual knowledge of named individuals after reasonable enquiry. Add an express "no buyer knowledge" clause.

### 8. Bluefen consent (cl. 3 / 6.3)
- **Facts:** Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue (around 30%). Change-control consent is under cl. 11.2, with conditions in cl. 11.3. Disclosure para 2 confirms that **no final consent and no evidence of satisfied conditions** existed as at 22 September.
- **Seller:** Says the consent is "addressed", but offers only reasonable endeavours, with the condition treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent.
- **Analysis:** "Addressed" contradicts the Seller's own disclosure. Consent-on-delivery ignores the cl. 11.3 conditions. A conditional consent that is never satisfied could still allow Bluefen to terminate after Completion. Reasonable endeavours is inadequate for a 30% customer.
- **Push back:**
  - Make it a Condition Precedent that is satisfied only by (a) an effective, unconditional (or conditions-satisfied) written consent from Bluefen, in a form reasonably acceptable to the Buyer, **and** (b) evidence that the cl. 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
  - The Condition should be waivable only by the Buyer.
  - Seller obligation upgraded beyond reasonable endeavours.
  - Request the current status of the consent now.

### 9. Riverlark facility (cl. 2 / 7)
- **Facts:** About AUD 3.2m outstanding (an approximate figure). Change-control is under cl. 8.1, discharge under cl. 9.2. Disclosure para 3 says the facility has not been repaid and no discharge is included.
- **Seller:** The release is to be provided after Completion.
- **Analysis:** A post-Completion release means we would complete with security still registered over the target. The change-control clause may also be triggered by Completion itself.
- **Push back:**
  - As Completion deliverables, require a current payout letter (a figure as at Completion, with daily interest), direct repayment from Completion funds, and executed deeds of release, PPSR releases and any mortgage or security discharges.
  - Treat the payout amount as Debt in the debt-free/cash-free mechanics.
  - A post-Completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark **and** Amelia Frost's approval. Neither exists.
  - Do not rely on the "approximately AUD 3.2m" figure. Get the payout letter.

### 10. DD-005 employee bonuses / funds flow
- **Facts:** AUD 420,000 in conditional Completion bonuses. Disclosure para 5 confirms they are **not** in the funds flow, and says nothing on payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs.
- **Seller:** The funds flow "reflects the agreed price mechanics", with bonuses described as "a matter for the Seller."
- **Analysis:** The price mechanics are not agreed. If the Company pays the bonuses after Completion, the cost falls on us. "A matter for the Seller" is not a legal obligation. On-costs (payroll tax, superannuation, possibly workers' compensation) could add a material amount on top of AUD 420k. This is exactly the silent exclusion the playbook targets.
- **Push back:**
  - Either (a) include AUD 420k plus all triggered on-costs as a specific line item in the funds flow, treated as Debt or a Transaction Expense deducted from the price and paid through payroll at Completion; or (b) make them expressly Seller-funded, with an indemnity.
  - Require confirmation of the on-cost calculation.
  - Remove "agreed" from any description of the funds flow.

### 11. Ironquay IP (cl. 11.1)
- **Facts:** DD-004 cl. 7.3 makes transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials conditional on cleared payment of all SOW3 fees. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open. That is not independent proof either way. There is no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment.
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is "adequate."
- **Analysis:** Paying AUD 180k may not resolve the issue. The real risk is that the Company does not own the SOW3 Project Materials. That creates infringement, ownership and remediation exposure well beyond the fee.
- **Push back:**
  - Broaden the indemnity to cover all loss arising from any failure of the Company to own, or hold a sufficient licence to, the Ironquay deliverables. That includes third-party claims and re-development or remediation costs.
  - Keep the SOW3 cure: the Seller procures cleared payment, with evidence, and a confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay, ideally pre-Completion.
  - Keep this outside the general cap, thresholds and knowledge bar.
  - Do not concede that AUD 180k is owed or paid. Verify with bank evidence or Ironquay confirmation.

### 12. DD-006 export / privacy incident (cl. 4.6 / Schedule 6)
- **Facts:** A download link was sent to an unintended external address. The export may contain about 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, timestamps). It is not established whether anyone accessed the file, what the exact scope is, or whether notification is required. The investigation is preliminary.
- **Seller:** "Not expected to be material."
- **Analysis:** That characterisation is unsupported, so we should not accept it. Equally, we must **not** overstate the matter. There is no confirmed breach, harm, notification obligation or quantified loss, and we should not demand a numeric amount. The right approach is process protection while the facts develop.
- **Push back:**
  - Pre-Completion covenants: preserve all logs and evidence, continue a proper investigation (consider independent forensic review), give the Buyer regular updates and access, and make no notification decisions or regulator or individual communications without consultation.
  - Require an assessment under the Privacy Act eligible data breach regime to be completed or progressed.
  - Delete the "not material" language.
  - Seek a specific indemnity for loss arising from the incident, regardless of disclosure, without assuming any outcome.
  - Request an updated status, since the information is six weeks old.

### 13. Sandbar supplier renewals (AUD 330,000)
- **Facts:** Three related renewals of AUD 110k each. The disclosure does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Seller:** "Ordinary-course operating costs."
- **Analysis:** This is an assertion. The playbook says to assess the renewals and neither classify them automatically as Debt nor demand a price deduction.
- **Push back:** Request the DD-008 and DD-011 contracts and the timing, scope, termination rights and accrual treatment, and confirm whether they were approved within budget and authority. Reserve our position on classification (ordinary course, Transaction Expense or Debt) pending that review. Do not concede "ordinary course" in the SPA.

### 14. Tax / IP warranties
- **Seller:** "Settled under the general regime."
- **Playbook:** OPEN. There is no resolution, and we are not assuming unlimited liability.
- **Push back:** Reject "settled". Tax and IP remain open items for separate negotiation, with their own regime (for example, a tax covenant with appropriate time limits) outside the general cap and thresholds. Make no concession that they fall under the general regime.

### 15. Title evidence
- **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the share register at DD-012.
- **Analysis:** DD-012 is an internal source supplied by the Seller. Disclosure para 10 itself acknowledges we have not verified it.
- **Push back:** Require independent evidence: an ASIC company extract and historical search consistent with the register, PPSR searches against the Seller and the Company, share certificates, and evidence of the issue and transfer history (including no options, convertibles or rights). Also require board and shareholder authority for the Seller, any security trustee or lender releases over the shares, and a clean title, capacity and authority warranty within the Fundamental regime.

### 16. Lower-priority confirmations
- **Office lease (DD-007):** Notification only, per the disclosure. Confirm independently, diarise the notice as a Completion deliverable, and confirm there is no change-of-control default.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** The assignment restriction is described as not triggered by a share sale. Verify against the clause text, including any change-of-control or deemed-assignment wording.

## Summary of recommendations

| # | Item | Seller position | Our response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | General cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | Counter 25% / AUD 6.0m. 20% is **not authorised** without Amelia Frost's written approval |
| 2 | Thresholds | AUD 25k / AUD 250k deductible | AUD 5k / AUD 50k, tipping basket from first dollar |
| 3 | Claims period | 18 months; limits apply to all Claims | 24 months; delete the "all Claims" override; 18 months not authorised |
| 4 | Fundamental/Title | Same as general | 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside thresholds, disclosure and knowledge |
| 5 | Fraud | Limited like everything else | Full carve-out from everything. Non-negotiable |
| 6 | Disclosure | Whole data room plus public records | Specific fair disclosure only |
| 7 | Buyer knowledge | Blanket bar incl. advisers and constructive knowledge | Delete; any qualifier limited to named Seller persons with reasonable enquiry |
| 8 | Bluefen | Reasonable endeavours; consent on delivery | CP: effective consent **and** evidence that cl. 11.3 conditions are met |
| 9 | Riverlark | Post-Completion release | Payout letter, repayment from funds, releases at Completion |
| 10 | Bonuses | Excluded from funds flow | AUD 420k plus on-costs as a line item or Seller-funded with indemnity |
| 11 | Ironquay | Narrow SOW3 indemnity | Broad IP indemnity plus SOW3 cure; AUD 180k unverified |
| 12 | DD-006 | "Not material" | Preserve logs, investigate, update covenants, specific indemnity; no assumed breach |
| 13 | Sandbar | Ordinary course | Assess; reserve classification |
| 14 | Tax/IP | "Settled" | Open; separate regime |
| 15 | Title | DD-012 register | Independent title, encumbrance and authority evidence |

**Process points for the deal team:**

1. **Do not concede the 20% cap or the 18-month period.** They match our fallbacks but are uncleared. If anyone wants to use either, seek Amelia Frost's written authority identifying this draft (the Seller Update draft and SPA-003), and use it only as part of a package that fixes items 3 to 7.
2. **Reject the characterisations.** The Seller's uses of "addressed", "agreed price mechanics", "adequate", "settled", "not material" and "ordinary course" are assertions. In several places (Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses) they are contradicted by the Seller's own Disclosure Letter.
3. **Refresh the facts.** The Disclosure Letter is dated 22 September 2026. Send a written request for current status on Bluefen, the Riverlark payout, Ironquay payment and assignment, the DD-006 investigation, the bonus on-costs and the Sandbar contracts. Record which updates are verified and which are Seller assertions.
4. **Prioritise in the mark-up.** The structural provisions come first, because they undermine everything else: the fraud carve-out, Fundamental/Title separation, deletion of the "all Claims" override, specific disclosure and deletion of the buyer-knowledge bar. Then the Completion deliverables (Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses), then the economic terms.

This is a negotiation analysis, not formal legal advice. The final mark-up should be settled by the responsible NSW-qualified lawyers on the deal team.
